messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic Solid-Phase Extraction (DMF-SPE) Using in Situ Formed Porous Polymer Monolith (PPM) Discs

REAGENTS USED:
  - C12 Casting Solution (butyl acrylate, 1,3-butanediol diacrylate, lauryl acrylate, and 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone photoinitiator in a 4:1:1 acetonitrile:ethanol:phosphate-buffer porogen; used to form the PPM disc)
  - Activation Solvent (0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile, 5 uL droplets)
  - Equilibration/Wash Solvent (0.5% v/v formic acid in deionized water, 5 uL droplets)
  - Sample (fluorescamine-labeled peptide or fluorescein analyte, 1 uL droplet)
  - Elution Solvent (500 mM sodium borate at pH 9.0, or 0.1% v/v formic acid in acetonitrile, 5 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1. PPM Disc Formation: Dispense a 1 uL droplet of C12 casting solution onto the device, translate it to a central actuation electrode, and cure it by UV irradiation (100 W, 365 nm, 5 min) to form a circular porous polymer monolith disc in situ.
2. Activation: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of activation solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 1 min, then actuate the droplet away to a waste reservoir.
3. Equilibration: Dispense a fresh 5 uL droplet of equilibration solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 1 min, then actuate the droplet away to waste.
4. Sample Loading: Dispense a 1 uL sample droplet, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, incubate 2 min (optimized loading time), then actuate the droplet away to waste.
5. Monolith Washing: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of wash solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to waste; repeat this wash cycle a second time (2 x 5 uL total).
6. Elution: Dispense a 5 uL droplet of elution solvent, actuate it back and forth across the PPM disc five times, then move it to a collection spot; repeat this elution cycle a second time so that two eluate droplets are pooled (optimized elution volume).
7. Detection: Interrogate the pooled eluate droplet for fluorescence intensity (lambda_ex/lambda_em as appropriate for the analyte) using a plate reader, or alternatively analyze the eluate by nanoESI-MS, to quantify the extracted/recovered analyte relative to a non-extracted control; then discard the analyzed droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful DMF-SPE performance is confirmed by an extraction efficiency (93 +/- 14% for a fluorescamine-labeled peptide) comparable to that of commercial C18 ZipTips (92 +/- 5%), successful preparative sample cleanup (recovery of MS signal for angiotensin II after removal of NaCl salt matrix or Pluronic F68 surfactant that otherwise fully suppressed the [M+H]+ signal), and a demonstrated sample-concentration factor of ~9 (12 uL sample eluted into 1 uL), supporting use of the method for on-chip desalting, surfactant removal, and preconcentration ahead of downstream analysis.

metadata.protocol_name: In Situ Porous Polymer Monolith Formation for Digital Microfluidic Solid-Phase Extraction (Yang et al. 2011)

sources.title: A Digital Microfluidic Method for in Situ Formation of Porous Polymer Monoliths with Application to Solid-Phase Extraction

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's four-step Standard Digital Microfluidic Solid-Phase Extraction Process (Methods section), preceded by the in situ PPM disc formation step (Figure 1b), and covering activation/equilibration (Figure 2a), sample loading (Figure 2b), monolith washing (Figure 2c), and elution (Figure 2d), with the optimized parameters (2 min sample incubation, two 5 uL wash droplets, two pooled 5 uL elution droplets) taken from the process-optimization results (Figure 3). Because BioScript has no primitive for a persistent, stationary solid-phase substrate (the PPM disc itself remains fixed in place on-chip while droplets are actuated across it, rather than being merged away), the PPM is modeled as a single flowing droplet handle ('ppm') that is repeatedly reassigned to the output of each successive mix, so that the same logical entity is threaded through activation, equilibration, loading, washing, and elution rather than being re-dispensed fresh at each step (unlike the DBS punch translation, where the immobile substrate was instead modeled by re-dispensing the substrate manifest at each step). Likewise, because BioScript's grammar exposes no dedicated 'UV cure' primitive, the paper's 100 W/365 nm, 5 min UV-initiated polymerization of the casting-solution droplet into a PPM disc is modeled using 'heat ... for 5m' as a stand-in, representing generic in-place curing rather than an actual thermal process. The final 'detect fluorescence' / threshold branch stands in for the plate-reader or nanoESI-MS quantification of extracted analyte described in the paper, using the ~20% relative-fluorescence cutoff observed for under-incubated (2 min) loading in Figure 3a as an illustrative pass/fail threshold rather than a value taken from a single explicit QC criterion in the text.

chemical_evidence.source_quote: A C12 casting solution was prepared by mixing 279 uL of butyl acrylate, 150 uL of 1,3-butanediol diacrylate, 69 uL of lauryl acrylate, 2.5 mg of 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone
activation solvent was 0.1% (v/v) formic acid in acetonitrile
equilibration and wash solvents were 0.5% (v/v) formic acid in deionized water
elution solvent was 500 mM sodium borate in deionized water at pH 9.0 ... or 0.1% (v/v) formic acid in acetonitrile

operation_evidence.source_quote: a 1 uL droplet of casting solution was dispensed ... polymerized by exposure to UV radiation (100 W, 365 nm, 5 min)

operation_evidence.source_quote: A PPM disc was activated by dispensing and driving a 5 uL droplet of activation solvent onto the monolith ... allowed to incubate on the disc for 1 min
operation_evidence.source_location: METHODS: Standard Digital Microfluidic Solid-Phase Extraction Process, Step 1

operation_evidence.bs_operation: ppm = mix ppm with s for 60s / heat ppm at 25c for 2m
operation_evidence.source_quote: A 1 uL sample droplet was dispensed and actuated to the PPM ... incubated for 2, 4, or 8 min

numeric_mismatches.field: ppm reassigned via chained mix rather than re-dispensed
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's PPM disc is a single physical monolith that stays fixed on-chip through all four steps while reagent droplets are actuated across it; BioScript has no persistent-substrate primitive, so the disc is modeled as one droplet handle threaded forward through successive 'mix' reassignments rather than a truly stationary object.

This models UV-initiated photopolymerization (100 W, 365 nm), not an actual thermal cure at 25 C; 'heat' is used only because it is the closest available BioScript primitive for a timed in-place process step.

The paper uses either a fluorescence plate reader (for fluorescein/fluorescamine-peptide analytes) or nanoESI-MS (for underivatized peptides), not a single generic threshold; the <=20 cutoff is illustrative, adapted from the ~20% relative-fluorescence result reported for 2 min sample loading (Figure 3a), rather than an explicit pass/fail criterion stated in the text.

numeric_mismatches.field: sample-concentration (Figure 5, ~9x concentration factor) and preparative-cleanup nanoESI-MS validation (Figure 4, NaCl/Pluronic F68 removal)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled as separate branches. These are alternate downstream-analysis/validation experiments run on the same core four-step DMF-SPE procedure rather than additional protocol steps, and are captured qualitatively in the natural-language description's INTERPRETATION section rather than as distinct BioScript operations.
